svg.title: Efficient Scaledown: the four capabilities and what each one solves
svg.desc: Efficient Scaledown architecture in Microsoft Fabric Spark: Breaking the shuffle-to-executor coupling via Remote Shuffle Manager, Shuffle Migration, Decision Layer, and AQE Shuffle Write, with measured benchmark gains and platform adoption constraints.
svg.text: Efficient Scaledown — The Four Capabilities & Architecture
Breaking the executor-to-shuffle coupling: Remote Shuffle Manager, Shuffle Migration, Decision Layer & AQE Write
STAGE 1: THE STRUCTURAL PROBLEM & UPSTREAM FOUNDATION

g.aria-label: Shuffle output is glued to local disk
g.title: Shuffle output is glued to local disk — Shuffle data on executor-local disk blocks safe scale-down and risks stage recompute.
g.text: 1 · Shuffle Output is Glued to Local Disk
• Shuffle data written to local disk blocks scale-down until downstream stages finish
• Releasing node prematurely triggers FetchFailedException & full stage recompute
• Forces capacity administrators to choose between paying for idle VMs vs job failures

g.title: Spark's own partial answer — Spark's graceful decommissioning and pluggable shuffle IO are the foundation Fabric builds on.
g.text: • Pluggable shuffle IO interface (spark.shuffle.sort.io.plugin.class) enables external routing
• Upstream defaults to false and lacks per-stage cloud-native routing intelligence

svg.text: STAGE 2: THE FOUR INTERLOCKING FABRIC CAPABILITIES

g.title: Remote Shuffle Manager — Remote Shuffle Manager writes shuffle data to Blob Storage instead of local disk.
Shuffle Migration — Shuffle Migration moves locally held blocks to a peer before an executor exits.
Decision Layer — The Decision Layer routes large shuffles remotely and keeps small ones local.
AQE Shuffle Write — AQE Shuffle Write shapes the blocks handed to remote shuffle storage.

svg.text: STAGE 3: MEASURED BENCHMARK IMPACT & ADOPTION CONSTRAINTS

g.title: What Microsoft measured — Microsoft reports a 54% compute reduction and up to 57% faster runtime from per-stage routing.
g.text: • Benchmark: TPC-DS suite executed on Spark 4.1 in unified multi-query session
• Total Compute: Dropped from 14,952 down to 6,880 VM-minutes (54% savings)
• Per-stage hybrid routing was up to 57% faster than naive 100% remote shuffle

g.title: Constraints that gate adoption — Efficient Scaledown requires the native engine and explicit configuration to enable.
g.text: • Runtime Requirement: Requires Fabric Spark Runtime 3.5+ (or Runtime 2.0+)
• Native Engine Prerequisite: Must have Native Execution Engine enabled (spark.native.enabled)
• Explicit Activation: Disabled by default; must configure pool / workspace properties
• Storage Account Topology: Requires separate Azure Blob Storage without HNS (practitioner rule)

svg.text: Fabric Codex — Original Diagram, August 2026. Sourced from Microsoft Fabric Blog & Apache Spark Decommissioning Documentation.
